item.text: I’m reviewing from memory only and will save new, distinct candidates in `followup.tsv`; I won’t open or alter the prior TSV.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec13/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.34.11	repayment according to work and way	The commentary makes each person answer for work at the appointed reckoning; Job says God repays a person according to his work and makes each find according to his way, a direct formulation of individual moral accounting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.16.2	God weighs spirits	The commentary's scales test deeds; Proverbs adds that God weighs the spirits behind a person's apparently pure ways, bringing motive as well as outward action under scrutiny.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.62.13	repaid according to each one's work	The commentary's deficient account rests on work; this verse says God repays each person according to his work, supplying a distinct recompense formula in the psalm whose earlier verse weighs humanity on scales.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.3.17	time to judge every work	The commentary connects time with the due day and says good and bad works are separated; Ecclesiastes explicitly says there is a time for every matter and work when God judges righteous and wicked.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.7.10	court sits; books opened	The commentary says deeds are present at judgment; Daniel's heavenly court takes its seat and opens books, adding a courtroom and record-book scene distinct from Daniel's weighed king and resurrection.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.12.1	names written in the book	The commentary distinguishes those who escape loss; Daniel says those found written in the book are delivered during unparalleled trouble, adding a register of the spared immediately before the resurrection division.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.3.10	righteous eat fruit of deeds	The commentary's exception is marked by righteous work; Isaiah tells the righteous it will be well because they will eat the fruit of their deeds, tying outcome to the person's own conduct.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.3.11	wicked receive their deeds	The commentary's loss and punishment follow bad work; Isaiah gives the converse verdict that it will go badly for the wicked because what their hands have done is repaid to them.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.98.9	world judged in righteousness	The commentary's accounting concerns every person; the psalm pictures the Lord coming to judge the world and peoples with righteousness and equity, extending judgment to the whole inhabited world.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Mal.3.16	book of remembrance	The commentary says each person's work is present at judgment; Malachi describes a record written before God for those who fear him and esteem his name, preserving the words and deeds of a faithful group.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.11.9	joy now; judgment for all	The commentary treats time as a term ending in reckoning; Ecclesiastes permits the young to follow heart and eyes but warns that God will bring them into judgment for all this, joining present action to future accounting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.9.10	work only within mortal life	The commentary makes the present term the span in which work counts; Ecclesiastes urges doing what one's hand finds with strength because there is no work or knowledge in Sheol, making life's limit a reason for action.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Dan.7.10	heavenly books and verdict	The commentary's balance accounts for deeds; Daniel's opened books belong to a heavenly tribunal before dominion is taken from beasts and given to the holy ones, adding a cosmic verdict and transfer of rule.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	4 Ezra (2 Esdras) 7:35	judgment, truth, recompense, awakened deeds	The commentary joins truth, work, and final recompense; 4 Ezra's end-time vision says judgment remains, truth stands, reward is shown, and good and evil deeds awaken, making the moral record explicit at the end.
strong	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:22	life ends in an account before the King	The commentary brings each human to the term of an account; Avot says every person is born, lives, dies, and must give account before the King of kings, compressing life's whole course into an unavoidable reckoning.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Shabbat 31a	questions at heavenly judgment	The commentary makes faith and work answerable at the end; the Talmud imagines the court asking whether one dealt faithfully, fixed time for Torah, hoped for salvation, and pursued wisdom, turning judgment into concrete questions about a lived life.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.18.25	judge of all earth; righteous not swept with wicked	The commentary says humanity is in loss but preserves an exception; Abraham asks whether the Judge of all earth will destroy the righteous with the wicked, making the justice of a collective sentence depend on distinguishing the righteous.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.90.8	secret sins exposed	The commentary says deeds are found present at reckoning; the psalm says God sets iniquities and hidden sins before his face, adding the exposure of what a person conceals.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.11.9	mortal pleasure under judgment	The commentary reads the counted time as a deadline; Ecclesiastes' warning to the young makes even their private choices answerable, a specific bridge from finite life to judgment.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Arakhin 16b	limits and difficulty of rebuke	The commentary's mutual counsel in truth recalls Leviticus' command to rebuke a neighbor; the rabbis debate whether people know how to give or receive rebuke, showing how the duty can fail in practice.
medium	tevrat	motif	4 Ezra (2 Esdras) 7:33	seat of judgment; patience ends	The commentary describes a due day that closes the account; 4 Ezra says the Most High appears at the seat of judgment as compassion and long-suffering pass away, giving the end a sharper finality.
medium	tevrat	motif	Wisdom of Solomon 5:1	righteous stand boldly at judgment	The commentary's exception is the group not lost; Wisdom pictures the righteous standing with great confidence before those who afflicted them, adding vindication after apparent defeat.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.5.29	resurrection according to deeds	The commentary links resurrection and division by work; Jesus describes those who did good rising to life and those who did evil rising to judgment, joining conduct directly to the two outcomes.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.7.21	doing the Father's will	The commentary's exception includes belief and righteous deeds; Jesus says entry into the kingdom belongs to the one who does the Father's will, distinguishing verbal confession from enacted obedience.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.13.49	end-of-age separation	The commentary says good and evil are distinguished at the end; Jesus' net parable has angels separate the wicked from the righteous at the close of the age.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.13.50	evil cast into the fiery furnace	The commentary associates evil work with punishment by fire; the net parable ends with the wicked thrown into a fiery furnace, giving separation a specific punitive outcome.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.8.15	word kept; fruit borne with endurance	The commentary combines truth, good work, and patience; in the seed parable the good soil holds the word in an honest heart and bears fruit with endurance, bringing those elements together in one image.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.19.15	servants summoned to account	The commentary says each person's work is brought before the judge; in the minas parable the returning nobleman summons servants to learn what each gained in trade, a concrete audit of entrusted work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.19.17	work rewarded with authority	The commentary ties work to recompense; the servant praised for faithfulness in a small matter receives authority over cities, making reward proportionate to performed work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.4.5	hidden motives disclosed	The commentary says work is found present at judgment; Paul says the Lord will bring hidden things to light and disclose the intentions of hearts, adding inward motive to the public accounting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.7	sowing and reaping	The commentary frames work as a loss-and-recompense account; Paul says a person reaps what is sown and that God is not mocked, giving moral consequence the image of harvest.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.8	flesh or Spirit; corruption or life	The commentary divides bad and good work by their end; Paul contrasts sowing to the flesh, which reaps corruption, with sowing to the Spirit, which reaps eternal life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.9	patience until the due harvest	The commentary joins patience to good work before the term arrives; Paul tells the community not to grow weary in doing good because there will be a harvest at the proper time.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.10	God does not forget work and love	The commentary says deeds remain present at judgment; Hebrews says God is not unjust to forget the community's work and love shown in service to the saints, making faithful labor remembered.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.6.12	faith and patience inherit promise	The commentary's exception joins belief, righteous work, and patience; Hebrews urges imitation of those who inherit the promises through faith and patience.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.1.3	work of faith; labor of love; steadfast hope	The commentary's exception gathers faith, work, and patience in community; Paul remembers the Thessalonians' work produced by faith, labor prompted by love, and endurance grounded in hope.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.6	God repays affliction	The commentary says the day binds recompense to deeds; Paul calls it just for God to repay affliction to those who afflict the community, a reversal in which the persecutor receives the measure imposed.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.1.7	relief at the Lord's revelation	The commentary makes the appointed day the end of a period of loss; Paul promises relief to the afflicted when Jesus is revealed from heaven, pairing the same event with vindication for sufferers.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.4.5	account to the judge of living and dead	The commentary says every person meets the account; Peter says wrongdoers will give account to the one ready to judge the living and the dead, explicitly universalizing the reckoning.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.13	deeds follow the dead	The commentary says what people have done is present at judgment; Revelation blesses those who die in the Lord and says their deeds follow them, making work accompany a person beyond death.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.18.23	a king settles accounts	The commentary uses an account image for loss and recompense; Jesus begins a kingdom parable with a king settling accounts with servants, then develops how debt and mercy affect the verdict.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.18.34	forgiven debtor punished for withholding mercy	The commentary sorts deeds toward punishment or reward; in the parable a servant whose debt was forgiven is handed over after refusing mercy to another, making the treatment of one's neighbor decisive.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.12.48	the spoken word judges at the last day	The commentary makes truth something mutually upheld and deeds answerable at the end; Jesus says the word he has spoken will judge the hearer on the last day, specifying the received message as a standard.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.14.12	each gives account to God	The commentary brings each person to a personal reckoning; Paul says each of us will give an account of himself to God, stressing individual answerability within a dispute about judging fellow believers.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:James.1.15	sin completed brings death	The commentary warns of persistence in deeds that lead to fire; James describes desire giving birth to sin and fully grown sin bringing forth death, a specific account of how evil action reaches its outcome.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Pet.3.11	holy conduct while awaiting the Day	The commentary pairs the approaching term with work and patience; Peter asks what sort of people believers should be in holy conduct and godliness while awaiting the Day of the Lord.
medium	incil	motif	Justin Martyr, First Apology 12	everlasting outcome according to actions	The commentary's accounting divides people by what they do; Justin says people go to everlasting punishment or salvation according to the merit of their actions, an early Christian defense of judgment by conduct.
medium	incil	motif	Shepherd of Hermas, Mandate 5	patience as a practice of righteousness	The commentary makes patience part of the work that marks the exception; Hermas contrasts patience with short temper and connects endurance to right conduct, treating patience as morally active rather than passive delay.
EOF"
